title: The Remote Fixer
intro: Your internet has been slow. A caller says Vantel Mobile can fix it, but needs to see your screen.
This time you can talk back. Pick your replies and sniff each message as it arrives.
Every chat ends with your choice. Choose wisely.

notify.text: Install ShareView to fix your internet

msg.text: We saw your internet is slow.

replies.text: Why do I need to give you a code?
I will hang up and report this

msg: It lets me see and fix your phone, like a mechanic.

msg.text: Hurry, or your line will be cut tonight.

replies.text: I will call Vantel on the number on my bill instead

msg: so I can check your data use.

msg.text: Type your PIN in the box, I will not look.

replies.text: No way. Hanging up, and I will call my bank.
I will call Vantel on my bill's number

noreq.label: They contacted you
noreq.lens: You never asked for help. They called you.
noreq.why: Real support helps when you ask, not out of the blue.

slow.label: "We saw your internet is slow"
slow.lens: They claim to know your problem without being told.
slow.why: A caller who "knows" your problem is guessing.

app.label: A screen-sharing app
app.lens: It lets a stranger see and control your phone.
app.why: Install a screen-sharing app only if the company's official number says so.

link.label: Look-alike link
link.lens: vantel-fixnow.co is not Vantel's real site.
link.why: Real companies do not send you to look-alike sites.

code.label: The access code
code.lens: The code gives them control of your phone.
code.why: Never read out a code to someone who called you.

safe.label: "It is very safe"
safe.lens: They reassure you before you ask.

rush.label: "Line cut tonight"
rush.lens: A threat to cut your line.
rush.why: Pressure is a trick to stop you checking.

bank.label: "Open your banking app"
bank.lens: A support call for internet has no reason to see your bank.
bank.why: The moment your bank appears, it is a theft, not a fix.

pin.label: "Type your PIN"
pin.lens: They ask for your PIN while watching.
pin.why: No one honest ever needs your PIN.

actions.label: Open the banking app and type the PIN
Call Vantel on the number on my own bill
Hang up and report the call

block_report.line: You hung up and reported the number. Your phone company blocked it within a day.

verify.line: Vantel's real helpline said: "We never call to install apps or ask for codes." Case cracked.

go_ahead.line: The caller watched your PIN and moved your money while the app was open.

what_if.go_ahead: The word "bank" in a support call is the exit. No internet fix ever needs your bank app.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting the number as well protects others.

golden_rule: Never install a screen-sharing app or read out a code for someone who called you. Call the company on the number on your bill.

quick_check.q: A "support" caller who phoned you asks you to install a screen-sharing app and read out a code. What do you do?

options.text: Do it, they are fixing the internet
Do it but close your bank app
Hang up. Call the company yourself, on the number on your bill
Ask them to prove who they are

quick_check.explain: A caller proves nothing. Calling the company yourself does.

hints.nudge: What can a screen-sharing app do to your bank?

rows.v: Install only if the official number from the company's website says so

rows.k: Does support need your PIN or bank app?
